item.research_question: How can a high-entropy design strategy be utilized to simultaneously achieve ultrahigh recoverable energy storage density (Wrec) and ultrahigh efficiency (η) in lead-free relaxor ferroelectric ceramics?
item.material_system: Lead-free relaxor ferroelectrics with the composition [(K0.2Na0.8)0.8Li0.08Ba0.02Bi0.1](Nb0.68Sc0.02Hf0.08Zr0.1Ta0.08Sb0.04)O3 (KNN-H), based on the K0.2Na0.8NbO3 lattice.
item.processing_route: Conventional solid-state reaction method: starting powders were planetary ball-milled for 24 h, dried at 120 °C for 2 h, calcined at 800 °C for 5 h, mixed with 0.5 wt% PVB binder, pressed into pellets at 300 MPa, heated to 550 °C to burn out binder, and sintered at 1230 °C in closed crucibles for 2 h.
item.test_conditions: Electric fields up to 740 kV cm−1 for P-E loops; temperatures from 25 to 140 °C and frequencies from 1 to 300 Hz for stability tests; cycling up to 10^6 times; charge/discharge tests at 300 kV cm−1.
key_findings: A giant recoverable energy storage density (Wrec) of ~10.06 J cm−3 was achieved.
An ultrahigh energy storage efficiency (η) of ~90.8% was realized.
The breakdown electric field (Eb) was enhanced to 740 kV cm−1.
The Vickers hardness (Hv) reached ~7.70 GPa, significantly higher than pure KNN (~3.24 GPa).
The discharge energy density (WD) was ~3.26 J cm−3 with an ultrafast discharge rate (t0.9) of ~34 ns.
The material exhibited temperature-insensitive energy storage (Wrec ~3.38 ± 0.20 J cm−3) from 25 to 140 °C.
The material showed frequency-insensitive properties with Wrec ~4.46 ± 0.25 J cm−3 from 1 to 300 Hz.
Polarization vectors formed polar nanoregions (PNRs) with sizes of ~1–3 nm.
item.mechanism: The high-entropy strategy induces 'local polymorphic distortion' characterized by rhombohedral-orthorhombic-tetragonal-cubic (R-O-T-C) multiphase nanoclusters and random oxygen octahedral tilt. This structure creates a strong random field that reduces PNR size, delays polarization saturation, and drives the system back to a nonpolar state (near-zero Pr), resulting in slim P-E loops, high breakdown strength, and high efficiency.
item.limitations: The text does not explicitly state limitations of the study itself, though it notes that achieving Wrec ≥10 J cm−3 with η ≥90% simultaneously was a previous bottleneck in lead-free ceramics.
item.future_work: The authors propose that this high-entropy strategy opens an effective avenue to design dielectric materials with ultrahigh comprehensive energy storage performance to meet the demanding requirements of advanced energy storage applications.
quotes: A giant Wrec ~10.06 J cm−3 is realized in lead-free relaxor ferroelectrics, especially with an ultrahigh η ~90.8%.
The local polymorphic distortion can effectively reduce the size of polar nanoregions (PNRs) and further decrease the loss when working under a strong electric field.
